text:
[Council File 26-1425]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Been Held]
CIVIL RIGHTS, IMMIGRATION, SOCIAL SERVICES AND NEIGHBORHOODS COMMITTEE REPORT relative to the feasibility of expanding Opportunity L.A. to include an investment-based youth asset-building component that allows families to contribute funds that can grow over time and be used for post-secondary education, career or vocational training, or the purchase of a first home; and to identify appropriate account structures; and reporting on comparable children savings programs and best practices in other jurisdictions; and related matters.
Recommendation(s) for Council action, pursuant to Motion (Rodriguez - Blumenfield):
1. INSTRUCT the Community Investment Department (CID), with the assistance of the City Administrative Officer (CAO), Chief Legislative Analyst (CLA), City Attorney, and other relevant departments, and in consultation with the Los Angeles Unified School District and appropriate financial partners, to report to Council on the feasibility of expanding Opportunity L.A. to include an investment-based youth asset-building component that allows families to contribute funds that can grow over time and be used for post-secondary education, career or vocational training, or the purchase of a first home; and to identify appropriate account structures, including 529 plans, custodial investment accounts, savings accounts, or other legally permissible investment vehicles.
2. INSTRUCT the CID to report to Council on comparable children savings programs and best practices in other jurisdictions; opportunities to provide matching funds or incentives tied to milestones such as attendance, academic achievement, graduation, financial literacy, community service, internships, or workforce development, and potential public, philanthropic, financial institution, corporate, and community, partnerships to leverage City funding and family contributions.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
Neither the CAO nor the CLA has completed a financial analysis of this report.
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
summary: Council would ask the Community Investment Department to study expanding Opportunity L.A. with a savings component families could fund for college, job training or a first home, plus matching incentives and comparable programs elsewhere.
